### AI — The Growing Backlash

A fascinating sub-narrative emerged this week: **the AI backlash is real**. A r/technology post hit 4,500+ upvotes warning "The AI Backlash Could Get Very Ugly." Meanwhile:

- **Sam Altman** faces a court filing revealing he holds >$2B in companies doing business with OpenAI — self-dealing allegations from state AGs
- **OpenAI wants ChatGPT to access your bank accounts** — predictable privacy backlash
- **Power prices up 76%** in Eastern US directly attributed to AI data centers
- **Lake Tahoe residents given 1 year** to find new power as utility pivots to data centers

The infrastructure demands of AI are now creating **real-world externalities** that retail investors can see. This cuts both ways: it confirms demand is real (good for NVDA, CEG, AVGO), but it also creates regulatory and reputational risk (bad for sentiment momentum plays).

### Semiconductors — Tariff Roulette

The Beijing trip was supposed to produce a framework. It didn't. **No Taiwan agreement, no export control easing.** Semis sold off hard. Samsung's emergency production winddown before an 18-day strike (daily losses of $2B potential) adds supply-side pressure.

For MRVL and AVGO holders: this is noise unless tariffs escalate materially. The AI data center buildout is domestic (US-based hyperscalers). Taiwan exposure matters for manufacturing, but the demand signals remain astronomical.

### Cloud / SaaS — Cisco's Mixed Signal

Cisco's record revenue + layoff combo is the software industry in microcosm. Companies are buying infrastructure (good for networking, semi, power) but cutting internal costs (bad for software that doesn't justify itself). SaaS companies need to prove ROI in this environment.

## 🎓 Learning Corner — Breadth Divergence

**What is a breadth divergence?**

When the S&P 500 hits new highs but a significant portion of stocks in the index are below their 50-day moving average, that's a **breadth divergence**. The index is being pulled up by a small number of mega-caps (NVDA, AAPL, META) while the average stock is struggling.

**Why it matters:**
- **Healthy bull markets** have broad participation — most stocks go up together
- **Narrow markets** (low participation) are fragile — if the leaders stumble, there's nothing to catch the fall
- Currently: **Nearly half the S&P is below its 50-day MA** despite the index at 7,500

**Think of it like a soccer team:** If your star striker keeps scoring but the rest of the team is playing badly, you'll win a few games. But if the striker gets injured, you're in trouble because nobody else can step up.

**When to worry:** A breadth divergence that lasts 4-6 weeks often precedes a correction. Watch for the percentage of stocks above their 50-day MA — if it drops below 40% while the index is at highs, that's a warning signal.
